analyst_view.overall: Crystal Palace (21st) and Real Sociedad (20th) both have 5 points and sit just outside the play-off places, so both need a result. Palace sacked Pierre Sage and lost Thomas Frank's first game 3-2 at Coventry, their fifth league defeat in a row; they have conceded at least twice in 11 of 17 games, and Frank says that must be fixed. Adam Wharton is banned in Europe, Sarr, Riad and Tomiyasu are out, Mingueza is doubtful and Doucoure is not registered, while Pino and Mateta serve Premier League bans only and can play. Real Sociedad's squad list leaves out Aramburu (as the numbers assume, with Hector Fort at right-back), Barrenetxea, Odriozola and Yangel Herrera, and Sucic is fit. Norwegian referee Rohit Saggi (about 3.8 cards a game) is already counted; this morning's pages bring no new news, so the view stands. A late check (starting11) lists Sucic out ill and Lerma unavailable, but its lists mix up domestic bans (it has Pino banned) and the morning's squad news had Sucic travelling, so I treat that as unconfirmed and leave the view as it was.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals and already add 6.2% to Palace's side for Aramburu's absence, which the squad list confirms. Palace lose Wharton, their main passer, which the numbers do not know, but they concede a lot (two or more in 11 of 17 games) and Mateta and Pino are available, so the two pull opposite ways and I stay at 3.3.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.1 corners, already nudged up for Real Sociedad's 40 corners in their last six. Palace keep Pino and McNeil wide and Sociedad have Kubo, Guedes and the attacking left-back Sergio Gomez, so nothing points either way and I stay at 9.1.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards, already lifted for Palace's 15 bookings in six games and trimmed for referee Rohit Saggi's calm record (3.8 a game). Wharton, who often picks up cards, is out, but two sides level on points under a new Palace manager make for a tense game, so the two balance and I stay at 4.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.2 shots, with Real Sociedad's busy recent shooting (106 in six) already adding about 19% to their side. Palace's midfield without Wharton (Timber, Hughes and Kamada or Lerma expected) should build less, which the numbers do not see, so I shade it slightly, to about 26.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.4 shots on target, already a little lower for Palace's quieter recent attack. Palace's forwards Mateta, Strand Larsen and Pino are available and Sociedad have Oyarzabal, Kubo and a fit Sucic, so the finishers are mostly there and I stay at 9.4.
